newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Attorney says Merrill, Lazard probe continues.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Attorney says Merrill, Lazard probe continues.

text.p: U.S. Attorney Brien O'Connor said Thursday that federal probes into relationships between the municipal bond operations of Merrill Lynch & Co Inc and Lazard Freres & Co are continuing despite a conviction in August of a key player in the probe.

Mark Ferber, formerly an executive at Lazard, was convicted in August of 58 counts of fraud and corruption relating to a contract he maintained with Merrill to help the firm develop its municipal swaps business.

O'Connor, assigned to the public corruption and special prosections unit in the U.S. Attorney's Office in Boston, declined to comment further on the scope or timetable of the continuing investigation.

Speaking at a conference here sponsored by Grant's Municipal Bond Observer, O'Connor also said that the sentencing date for Ferber was moved to Nov 21 from Nov 4 because of a number of motions filed by the defense. The motions include one for acquittal and one for a new trial.
Discussing the groundbreaking case against Ferber, O'Connor said the probe has helped federal agents develop an expertise in the investigation of municipal finance.
"We now have more of an expertise, and as a result of this expertise, it is more likely we would conduct investigations in the future," O'Connor said.

The official said Ferber's conviction gave a "lift" to his office, and prompted calls from U.S. attorneys around the country and from staff at the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, who said they were "heartened" that a case of this complexity could be presented to a jury and a conviction result.
O'Connor also said that as a result of the probe, industry professionals have become more comfortable in speaking with federal agents about problems they see in the industry.
A number of market participants "really wanted the industry to be clean and fair," O'Connor said. "A lot of those people were helpful to us."

O'Connor said he could not speak about the need for more regulation in the municipal market but said new regulations requiring more disclosure of relationships between various players on a deal were "great."
